I'd start by checking the test layout, since I haven't seen it:

<command>ls tests pricing && ls tests | head -50</command>

I'm assuming `tests/` exists and has no `test_invoice_merging.py`. If the repo uses a different layout or already has an invoice test file, I'd put the tests there instead.

This test goes through the public API (`add`, `total`) only. It doesn't touch `_lines_by_sku`, so it keeps protecting `total()` if the storage changes again.

<edit path="tests/test_invoice_merging.py">
from decimal import Decimal

from pricing.invoice import Invoice


def test_empty_invoice_totals_zero():
    assert Invoice("c1").total() == Decimal("0")


def test_distinct_skus_are_summed():
    invoice = Invoice("c1")
    invoice.add("A", 2, Decimal("10.00"))
    invoice.add("B", 1, Decimal("0.10"))

    assert invoice.total() == Decimal("20.10")


def test_repeated_sku_at_same_price_sums_quantities():
    invoice = Invoice("c1")
    invoice.add("A", 2, Decimal("10.00"))
    invoice.add("A", 3, Decimal("10.00"))

    assert invoice.total() == Decimal("50.00")


def test_repeated_sku_at_different_prices_charges_each_add_at_its_own_price():
    invoice = Invoice("c1")
    invoice.add("A", 2, Decimal("10.00"))
    invoice.add("A", 3, Decimal("12.00"))

    # 2*10 + 3*12. Merging into one line must not reprice earlier adds
    # at the latest unit price (that would give 5*12 = 60).
    assert invoice.total() == Decimal("56.00")
</edit>

Run the new file:

<command>uv run pytest -q tests/test_invoice_merging.py</command>

These tests will pass immediately, because they characterize a refactor that already exists. So I can't watch them go red from missing code. Instead I'd confirm they can fail by temporarily introducing the bug a bad merge would cause, with a backup outside the repo since there's no git here:

<command>cp pricing/invoice.py /tmp/invoice.py.bak
sed -i '' 's/line\[1\] += qty \* unit_price/line[1] = line[0] * unit_price/' pricing/invoice.py
uv run pytest -q tests/test_invoice_merging.py
cp /tmp/invoice.py.bak pricing/invoice.py
diff /tmp/invoice.py.bak pricing/invoice.py && echo restored</command>

I expect `test_repeated_sku_at_different_prices_charges_each_add_at_its_own_price` to fail with 60 != 56 and the other three to pass. If it doesn't fail that way, the test is wrong and I'd fix it before going on. The `diff` must print `restored`, so I know the production file is back to your version.

Then the project's full suite, not just my file:

<command>uv run pytest -q</command>

Message to my partner:

> I added `tests/test_invoice_merging.py` with four tests that use only `Invoice.add` and `Invoice.total`, so they don't depend on the new dict storage. They cover the empty invoice, distinct SKUs, a repeated SKU at the same price, and a repeated SKU at different prices. The last one is the one that matters: it expects 56 (2×10 + 3×12), which catches a merge that reprices earlier quantities at the latest unit price.
>
> These passed on the first run, since the refactor was already in place, so I couldn't see them fail the usual way. To check they can fail, I temporarily changed the line-amount update in `add` to `line[1] = line[0] * unit_price`. The different-price test then failed as expected, and I restored `invoice.py` and confirmed with a diff that it matches your version.
>
> The expected values are computed by hand, because the old list-based implementation is gone and there's nothing to compare against. I'll paste the results of the full `uv run pytest -q` run, including any failures or skips I didn't cause. If `tests/` is organised differently from what I assumed, tell me where the file should go.

I can't report actual results until the commands run. I'd fill in the real pass/fail output from each run before sending this.
